function: p. 4: DeepReCE CNN channel estimation and IDLMuD LSTM NOMA multi-user symbol detection; main metric BER (p. 1), so area 1; power allocation by non-learned SSA (p. 7).
notes: Exclude, code system (Step 1, check 6), shown on p. 3. The learned parts are the DeepReCE CNN channel estimator and the IDLMuD LSTM multi-user detector (p. 4: "Joint channel estimation and multi-user signal detection are performed via DL"). The power allocation comes from a non-learned swarm metaheuristic (p. 7: "finding the optimal power allocation based on the Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA)"), so the learned method does no NTN resource, power, or beam control. The area is therefore 1, set by the main metric BER (p. 1; Figs. 7-11, pp. 11-12), not 6. The link is single-antenna at both ends, with no RIS: a single satellite beam (p. 2: "each satellite communicates with terrestrial users in its single-beam coverage area"), a scalar channel per subcarrier (p. 3, Eq. 2: "H_k,n and ω_k,n are the frequency response and noise variance of the channel from the LEO satellite to U_k,n"), and a channel estimate of size Nf × Nt × 2 used by scalar division (p. 5, Eq. 15: ŝ_k = y_k,n / Ĥ_k,n). The paper never states an antenna count, and Table I (p. 9) lists none. For the reviewer: I read "OTFS and NTN works admit single-antenna links" as meaning the works of areas 4 and 6. If it instead covers any work set in a satellite link, this work passes Step 1 as area 1 (LEO NOMA-OFDM downlink, trained and tested on multipath Rice, NTN-TDL-A and NTN-TDL-A with 6 kHz Doppler, p. 8; NTN-TDL-A is called TR 38.901 on p. 8, but reference [33] is TR 38.811, p. 14).
